cards.title: API key was rejected
cards.body: Check `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`: no quotes or spaces, not revoked, from the right workspace.

cards.title: Unexpected offline mode
cards.body: The key isn't visible to Python. Export it in the same terminal, or use `.env`.

cards.title: Rate limited
cards.body: Wait, reduce parallel requests, or raise `STUDY_MAX_RETRIES`.

cards.title: Cut-off answers or quizzes
cards.body: Raise `--max-tokens`, or ask for fewer questions.

items.q: How would you test code that calls an LLM API without spending money?
items.a: Put a **test double behind the real SDK**: a fake server (here an `httpx` MockTransport) that speaks the same protocol, so tests run the real client code, and can script errors, refusals and truncation.
items.trap: Mocking your own function so the SDK never runs. Then retries, streaming and parsing are never tested.

items.q: How do you stop an AI feature from running up a huge bill?
items.a: Measure tokens on every call, convert to cost, and **check a budget before each call**. Add `max_tokens`, step limits for loops, and alerts on spend.
items.trap: "We'll watch the dashboard." By the time you look, a loop may have spent the money.

items.q: Structured output passed validation. Is the content correct?
items.a: Not necessarily. The schema guarantees **shape**, not **truth**. You still check facts, business rules (e.g. the answer index points to a real option) and test with evals.

items.text: LLMs predict tokens; tokens drive cost, limits and speed

scenes.question: Why do output tokens matter so much for cost?
options: They usually cost several times more than input tokens
They don't count toward the context window
scenes.explain: On Claude Opus 5.5, output tokens cost $20 per million vs $4 for input: five times more. Ask for concise answers.

scenes.question: What does `stop_reason == "max_tokens"` tell you?
options: The reply was cut off at your limit and may be incomplete
The context window is full of history
scenes.explain: The reply hit `max_tokens` and stopped, possibly mid-sentence or mid-JSON. Raise the limit or ask for less.

scenes.question: A chat bot forgets everything said earlier. What's the most likely bug?
options: The app doesn't send the earlier messages with each request
scenes.explain: The API is stateless. The app must send the history (and store each reply) on every request.

scenes.question: Which errors are worth retrying automatically?
scenes.explain: Rate limits, server errors and network failures can recover. The Anthropic SDK retries them twice by default, with backoff.

scenes.question: What does `client.messages.parse(..., output_format=Quiz)` give you?
options: Plain text you must parse yourself
A guarantee the quiz is factually correct
scenes.explain: You get a validated object that matches the schema. Structure is guaranteed, **truth is not**: facts still need checking.
